source.what: the Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 260 (Limitation of Actions)
source.via: the Internet Archive's captures of the Legislature's own section pages, taken between September 2025 and October 2026

rows.clock: From the day the cause of action accrues. For a crash or a fall that is the day it happened.
rows.note: Covers every action of tort, and contract actions that seek damages for a personal injury, unless another section says otherwise.

rows.clock: From the death, or from when the executor or administrator knew or should have known the facts behind the claim.
rows.note: Brought by the executor or administrator, not by the family directly. Punitive damages of at least $5,000 are available for gross negligence or reckless conduct.

rows.clock: Three years from accrual, but never more than seven years after the act or omission.
rows.note: The seven-year cap does not apply when a foreign object was left in the body. Every case first goes before a three-member tribunal under c. 231, § 60B.

rows.clock: From the day the cause of action accrues.
rows.note: Massachusetts names assault and battery together and gives both the same three years. Maryland, by contrast, gives assault one year.

rows.clock: From the day the cause of action accrues.

rows.claim: Hit-and-run: notice to the police and the registrar
rows.clock: Written notice of the time, place and facts within 30 days of the crash. The lawsuit can then wait until six months after the driver is identified.
rows.note: No action under this section after three years from the crash, however late the driver is found.

rows.clock: Whichever ends later: 35 years from the abuse, or 7 years from when the survivor discovered, or should have discovered, that it caused an emotional or psychological injury.
rows.note: The clock does not start running until the child turns 18.

rows.clock: From the date the employee first became aware that the disability was caused by the job. For a death, four years from the death.
rows.note: Notice to the employer or insurer is due as soon as practicable, separately from the four-year claim.

rows.claim: Injury from a defective building or structure
rows.clock: Three years from accrual, and never more than six years after the improvement opened for use or was substantially completed and occupied.
rows.note: Covers design, planning and construction claims against architects, engineers and builders.
The car in a crash runs on the same three years as the people in it.
Massachusetts draws no line between written and oral contracts. A contract claim for a personal injury falls back to three years under § 2A.
Also covers bank notes and promissory notes signed before an attesting witness, when the original payee sues.
A consumer suing under c. 93A, § 9 must first mail a written demand for relief at least 30 days before filing.

rows.claim: Written claim to a public employer
rows.clock: Within two years of the day the claim arose, in writing, to the executive officer of the public employer.
rows.note: For a city or town it can go to the mayor, manager, city solicitor, town counsel or clerk; for the Commonwealth, to the Attorney General. Silence for six months counts as a denial.

rows.clock: From the day the cause of action accrued, and only after the written claim has been denied.

rows.claim: Notice of a defect in a public way
rows.clock: Written notice within 30 days of the injury to the county, city, town or person responsible for the road, naming the injured person and the time, place and cause.
rows.note: The lawsuit itself then has three years. A missing notice is no defense for an injury caused by snow or ice unless the defendant shows it was prejudiced. Section 19 says who the notice goes to.
Covers claims under any law protecting civil rights, including discrimination in employment and housing.

exceptions.name: A child's clock starts at 18
exceptions.text: When the injured person is a minor, the ordinary period runs from when the disability ends, so an injury claim from childhood can be filed until the 21st birthday. The written claim to a public employer is a separate requirement, and the statute that sets it has no exception for minors.

exceptions.name: Medical malpractice on a child has its own rule
exceptions.text: The general rule for minors does not apply. A child's malpractice claim has three years from accrual, except that a child hurt before age six has until the ninth birthday. In every case the claim ends seven years after the act, unless a foreign object was left in the body.

exceptions.name: Mental illness when the claim arose
exceptions.text: A person incapacitated by mental illness when the claim first accrues gets the ordinary period from when the incapacity ends.

exceptions.name: A defendant who lives outside Massachusetts
exceptions.text: Time the defendant spends residing outside the Commonwealth is left out of the count. The section does not revive a claim already barred by the law of the state where the person bringing it lived.

exceptions.name: Fraud that hid the claim
exceptions.text: When the person responsible fraudulently concealed the claim, the time before discovery does not count.

exceptions.name: The discovery rule, which the courts read into the statute
exceptions.text: The Supreme Judicial Court held that a claim accrues when the injured person knew or reasonably should have known that they were harmed by someone's conduct. For a crash or a fall that is almost always the day it happened. It matters for injuries that surface late, such as a missed diagnosis.

faq.q: What is the statute of limitations for personal injury in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Three years from the day the claim accrues, under M.G.L. c. 260, § 2A. For a crash or a fall that is the day it happened. Assault and battery run on the same three years, under § 4.

faq.q: How long do you have to file a wrongful death lawsuit in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Three years from the death, or from when the executor or administrator knew or should have known the facts behind the claim, under M.G.L. c. 229, § 2.

faq.q: What is the deadline for medical malpractice in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Three years from when the claim accrues, and never more than seven years after the act, under M.G.L. c. 260, § 4. For a child hurt before age six, the claim can be filed until the ninth birthday under c. 231, § 60D.

faq.q: Does the statute of limitations stop for a minor in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Yes. Under M.G.L. c. 260, § 7 the ordinary period runs from the 18th birthday, so most injury claims from childhood can be filed until 21. Medical malpractice follows c. 231, § 60D instead, and child sexual abuse claims have 35 years under c. 260, § 4C.

faq.q: How long do you have to sue a city, town or the Commonwealth in Massachusetts?
faq.a: A written claim to the public employer is due within two years under M.G.L. c. 258, § 4, and the lawsuit within three years. An injury from a defect in a public road or sidewalk needs written notice within 30 days under c. 84, § 18.
